$meta.purpose: Verifiable, TAG-ANCHORED pin of the upstream ggml/llama.cpp tree that the coverage roster denominator AND all opponent-resolution baselines are defined against. Replaces the prior anti-pattern (a bare SHA against an out-of-repo sibling checkout) which was neither third-party-verifiable nor CI-reproducible.
constitution: The pin is TAG-anchored (an upstream release tag), never a bare SHA in prose.

Switching the pin to a DIFFERENT upstream tree = open a NEW epoch + re-run the T-N noise floor + the opponent-resolution probe; every measurement cell pinned to the old fingerprint goes STALE per the experiment constitution.
Local ggml patches are ONLY allowed as versioned .patch files applied by a build script. A dirty checkout is forbidden (it makes every baseline irreproducible).
CI and any third party MUST fetch upstream at the tag and verify sha == this file's sha before trusting any baseline (see .trellis/scripts/fetch_ggml_pin.py).

verified.verify_note: git -C <clone-of-upstream_url> fetch --tags origin && git rev-parse b9652^{commit} == 6eab47181cbd3532c88a105682b81b4729ab809b (confirmed, no describe offset -> the tag points EXACTLY at the SHA).

epoch_reasoning: Re-anchoring from the prior bare SHA to tag b9652 did NOT move the tree: b9652 == 6eab471 exactly (git describe, zero offset). Therefore the epoch stays 1 and NO re-probe is required -- and none is possible to invalidate, since no T-N noise floor or opponent probe has been run yet (this is the cheapest possible moment to harden the pin, exactly as instructed). A future move to a different tree WILL bump the epoch per the constitution above.
